title: Steady SLEW tokens/sec saturation harness for core models
creator: Rohit Kapoor
description: Goal: Build and operationalize a compact, reproducible tokens-per-second microbenchmark suite ("SLEW": Sustained Load, Edge microbursts, Latency warmup) for Redwood's core serving models that detects regressions in throughput and p95 latency. Scope includes test harness code, workload generators (sequence-shape profiles and KV cache modes), stable baselines, CI gating, alerting thresholds, and integration with Datadog/Grafana dashboards and the regression-bisect pipeline. This ticket covers implementation of the harness prototype, creation of canonical workload recipes, and onboarding three representative models (small/medium/large) to the suite.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run reproducible sustained runs for 3 model sizes with configurable batch_size, sequence_length_distribution, and request_rate
p95 and tokens/sec metrics computed with stable sampling windows and stored in Datadog/Grafana with a retained baseline snapshot for 90 days
Regression detector flags >10% tokens/sec drop or >20% p95 increase vs baseline and opens an automated regression ticket with attached artifacts
CI integration: nightly baseline job and PR gating check that fails on >5% regression for changed runtime codepaths
Workload recipes include: cold-KV warmup, hot-KV steady-state, microburst (1s spike), and long-tail steady-state with variable sequence mix
Runbook and onboarding doc checked into Confluence and linked from Console playbooks

run_instructions: 2) Prepare credentials: export RW_API_KEY and set BENCH_TARGET (model identifier)
3) Example: python run_harness.py --model model-x-small --duration 900 --seq-profile long-tail --kv-mode hot --batch 8
notes_and_tradeoffs: We intentionally keep the suite compact (few canonical profiles) to reduce noisy variability across environments; long tail of custom workloads will live in a separate repo for teams with bespoke needs.
Decision: use rolling median over 5-minute windows for tokens/sec to reduce sensitivity to short transient spikes; p95 computed on request latency samples per 1-minute buckets.
Tradeoff: Dedicated pool for benchmarks increases infra cost but provides more stable signal; mitigation: schedule runs during off-peak hours and use small GPU types for small/medium models.
